claims.text: Adding neodymium to an as-cast magnetic high-entropy alloy will increase its coercive field.
The intervention is addition of 2 at.% Nd.
Nd addition induces or enhances magnetic anisotropy in the alloy.
The Nd-induced modification of magnetic anisotropy causes increased coercivity.
At room temperature, 2 at.% Nd will produce a 20% increase in coercive field relative to the Nd-free as-cast baseline.
The Nd-free as-cast baseline alloy has a coercive field of 500 Oe.
A 20% increase over the stated 500 Oe baseline corresponds to a predicted coercive field of 600 Oe.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should hold for Nd additions up to 5 at.%.
The effect is expected under room-temperature hysteresis measurements using applied fields up to 10 kOe.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Grain size and phase distribution may also affect coercivity, but their roles are not fully understood in the proposed system.
The hypothesis is falsified if the Nd-added alloy's coercive field is less than 10% higher than that of the matched baseline.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is a 20% increase, but the falsification threshold is only a 10% increase. Thus, a result between 10% and 20% would fail to achieve the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
